department: Biomedical and Environmental Health Sciences (PhD), College of Arts & Sciences

deadline.value: Fall priority admission deadline is January 15 (no spring or summer admission).

gre_general.value: GRE scores can be submitted but are not required.
gre_general.quote: GRE can be submitted but is not required

gre_subject.value: ETS offers no GRE Subject Test in Biomedical Sciences, Chemistry, Biology, or Environmental Science, and GRE is not required for BEHS.
gre_subject.quote: GRE can be submitted but is not required

also.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Statement of Purpose must name prospective faculty mentor(s) of interest and the curriculum includes BEHS-720 Lab Rotation, but pages do not state whether prior advisor agreement is required before applying.

also.quote: *Statement of Purpose should include the names of the faculty mentor(s) you would like to work with and a description of your research interests, experiences, and career goals.

funding.value: All applicants are automatically considered for merit scholarships; CAS awards a limited number of graduate doctoral awards on a competitive basis.
funding.quote: All applicants automatically considered for merit scholarships.

also.quote: A limited number of graduate doctoral awards are available on a competitive basis. All doctoral applicants are automatically considered.

entry_route.value: Full graduate admission requires an earned U.S. baccalaureate degree or an international equivalent to a four-year U.S. bachelor's degree (alternative pathway via 3.30+ master's GPA or 3.50+ in last 12 graduate credits).
entry_route.quote: Applicants must hold either an earned baccalaureate degree from a nationally accredited institution or a degree equivalent to a four-year U.S. baccalaureate degree from an international institution with a similar level of accreditation or recognition by its home country.

notes: Multidisciplinary PhD offered by the Department of Biology in partnership with Chemistry and Environmental Science (41 credits plus dissertation; full-time or part-time).
